html:
SMTO-GML-0005 — SMTO couldn't find the email attachment

GUID: f1ed73ea-68d3-40d8-af01-a3fa782793d8
Slug: gmail-attachment-not-found
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • SMTO couldn't find a file it needed for this email, either a file to attach or an attachment on a message in your mailbox. No email was sent or drafted because of this step.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. If you wanted to send a file, select Add context under the message box, choose Add files to conversation, and attach the file again. SMTO can only attach files that were added to this conversation.
  2. If the file came from another task or conversation, ask SMTO to save it in this conversation first, then ask it to send the email again. A file from somewhere else isn't available until it's part of this conversation.
  3. If you wanted to save an attachment from an email, ask SMTO to open that email again and list its attachments, then pick one from that list. The email may have changed or been deleted, so the old reference to its attachment no longer matches.
  4. Open the email in Gmail and check the attachment is still there. If the attachment or email was removed, there is nothing left for SMTO to get.

What success looks like

  • SMTO shows the email with the right file attached, or the downloaded attachment appears as a file in the task.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO, with the name of the file or email you wanted. Don't send the email without the file just to get past this.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Gmail attachment resolution failed: an outgoing file reference is not granted to this conversation or cannot be read, an inline MIME attachment part has no usable data, or the requested attachment ID is not present on the current message.

What this means

  • Outgoing granted-file resolution fails, inline MIME attachment lookup cannot find usable bytes, provider lookup reports a missing attachment, or download finds no matching attachment metadata. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Outgoing granted-file resolution fails, inline MIME attachment lookup cannot find usable bytes, provider lookup reports a missing attachment, or download finds no matching attachment metadata.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish outgoing artifact/upload references from incoming message/attachment IDs and confirm account ownership.

How to fix it

  • For outgoing mail, confirm each attachment reference is a context:// or artifact:// item granted to this conversation (or a path the artifact publisher can stage); for downloads, re-read the message and use an attachment_id from its current attachment list. Do not reuse an identifier from an older read after the message or draft changed.
  • Refresh the exact message and attachment identifier.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The exact intended attachment is resolved from its authorized source.

What not to do

  • Do not submit a stale identifier or revision after another actor changed the resource.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
